key_insight: Gas-surface scattering laws can be amplified, muted, or even reversed by collisional feedback in rarefied hypersonic flow, so wall-response trends do not directly map to macroscopic forces and heat transfer.
engineering_relevance: For high-speed vehicle design, accurate prediction of drag, lift, and heating in rarefied regimes requires accounting for both accommodation physics and the evolving incident molecular population.
method: Direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) for hypersonic flow over a 40° inclined flat plate
Compare Maxwell and Cercignani-Lampis-Lord (CLL) scattering using fixed-incidence moment references
Re-evaluate alternative kernels on the same recorded non-reactive incident populations
evidence_signal: Across four benchmark Knudsen numbers (0.023 to 8.439), the study found up to 40% deviation from diffuse-specular interpolation at low Kn and a 3.1% diffuse-heat-transfer defect even at the highest Kn.
watch_item: Agreement in selected force or heat-transfer components does not prove common incidence or free-molecular behavior, so kernel calibration must avoid over-interpreting partial response matches.
paper_title: Gas-surface scattering and collisional feedback in rarefied hypersonic flow past an inclined flat plate
